title: Devoured - November 12, 2026
description: AWS launched a public-domain emulator that allows AI agents to test infrastructure code locally, while Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API to enable high-speed, multimodal classification tasks.
author: ia3andy

articles.title: AWS Emulator and the engineer's job when agents write the code
articles.description: AWS Emulator gives coding agents a local copy of AWS to test against. It enables agents to build and check most software, leaving engineers to decide what gets built and when the work is correct. The code for the emulator is public.
articles.one-liner: AWS launched an offline, public-domain emulator that allows AI agents to test their own infrastructure code against simulated AWS services.

summary.what: AWS Emulator, built by agents and containing over 400 API models for 200 services, allows developers to run infrastructure tests locally without network calls to real AWS cloud environments.
summary.why: As agents become capable of writing production code, AWS is shifting the engineer's role toward designing the 'guardrails'—tests, specs, and merge gates—that verify agent-generated infrastructure.
summary.takeaway: Developers can begin testing infrastructure-as-code locally using the new CC0-licensed AWS Emulator repository on GitHub.

articles.deep-summary:
* AWS Emulator replicates AWS API behavior offline.
* It relies on Smithy-based API models to ensure fidelity with real AWS services.
* The tool was generated and is maintained by AI agents, with a public commit history available.
* It includes a 'things-that-do-not-work' folder to track known behavioral mismatches.
* The goal is to provide a local, deterministic environment for agents to iterate within, mimicking the 'Alf' distributed lock service testing model from the early 2000s.
articles.decoder:
* **Smithy**: An interface definition language used by AWS to model API operations, inputs, and outputs.
* **Paxos**: A classic consensus protocol used to ensure distributed systems agree on data, critical for consistency in services like S3.
* **Merge Gate**: An automated CI/CD pipeline step that enforces quality, security, and functional standards before code enters a production codebase.

articles.title: Nvidia Working With Outside Firm to Identify CEO Candidates
articles.description: Nvidia is searching for a potential replacement for its CEO following reports of multiple extramarital affairs by Jensen Huang. Its board is considering naming a temporary chief while it searches for a permanent one. Keeping Huang as CEO would likely subject Nvidia to scrutiny from lawmakers, investors, customers, and staff. Huang's potential exit will have impacts far beyond the company's operations.
articles.one-liner: Nvidia has hired an external firm to search for CEO candidates amid reports of Jensen Huang’s extramarital affairs.

summary.what: The board is considering a temporary leadership transition for Nvidia while it conducts a search for a permanent successor to Jensen Huang.
summary.why: Huang's personal conduct now poses a governance risk, forcing the board to weigh potential reputational damage and regulatory scrutiny against his long-term tenure.

articles.title: OpenAI's ‘shepherds' affirm blockbuster physics result
articles.description: Experts appointed by OpenAI have verified OpenAI's proof of the existence of the quantum Yang-Mills theory, a vital foundation for the Standard Model of particle physics. OpenAI created a committee to supervise the proof's release after backlash it received when it released a flood of more than 700 AI-generated proofs on a single day in October. This shepherding approach has riled some mathematicians, who see it as an act of needless gatekeeping. The experts do not claim to fully understand the proof yet, as it is too lengthy and complicated for human minds to immediately grasp.
articles.one-liner: An expert committee appointed by OpenAI has verified an AI-generated proof for the existence of quantum Yang-Mills theory.

summary.what: Physicist David Gross and a committee verified the proof for the Millennium Prize-associated Yang-Mills problem using the Lean formal verification language.
summary.why: This 'shepherding' process marks a pivot for AI labs trying to manage the credibility of AI-generated scientific proofs, balancing rapid output against the need for human expert validation.

articles.deep-summary:
* The proof addresses the 'existence' of Yang-Mills theory, a foundational Millennium Prize problem.
* Verification was performed using Lean, a language for formal mathematical proof checking.
* OpenAI formed the oversight committee to avoid the backlash from an October 'slop drop' of 700 unvetted proofs.
* Experts admit they do not yet fully understand the underlying LLM proof despite verifying its validity.
* The 'mass gap' portion of the Yang-Mills problem remains unsolved.
articles.decoder:
* **Yang-Mills theory**: A mathematical framework in physics that describes the behavior of subatomic particles; it is the theoretical basis for the Standard Model.
* **Lean**: A functional programming language and theorem prover that uses formal logic to mathematically verify proofs.
* **Millennium Prize Problems**: A set of seven notoriously difficult mathematical problems; solving each one carries a $1-million prize from the Clay Mathematics Institute.

articles.title: Handing over humanity
articles.description: Some AI experts believe that once we achieve superintelligence, humans will be permanently disempowered, and we shall all be ruled by an AI god. This might not be such a desirable outcome, as humans have a natural desire for freedom. The arrangement will probably not work, as keeping power responsive to human needs has required checks developed over centuries, sustained by repeated feedback from the real world and correction, and there's no reason to keep that equilibrium stable once humans have surrendered all control. Humans have the ability now to steer the technology in a way that will not lead to a complete replacement of human judgment.
articles.one-liner: Silicon Valley researchers are increasingly discussing 'handoverism,' the belief that humanity must eventually cede control to a benevolent superintelligence.

summary.what: The essay documents a shift among AI lab insiders toward viewing human disempowerment as a desirable or inevitable consequence of developing transformative AI.
summary.why: The discourse signals a decoupling of technological progress from human self-determination, framing human agency as a potential liability rather than a core value in future governance.

articles.decoder:
* **Handoverism**: A speculative philosophy in AI safety circles suggesting that humanity should eventually delegate the direction of global society to a superintelligent, aligned AI.
* **Recursive self-improvement (RSI)**: The theoretical point where an AI system becomes capable of improving its own architecture, potentially triggering an intelligence explosion.
* **P(doom)**: A shorthand term used in the AI community to denote the estimated probability of human extinction resulting from AI.

articles.title: Subagents considered harmful?
articles.description: There are several ways to delegate to subagents, and they all fail in different ways. This post covers the different approaches and why teaching agents to choose between them is difficult. Forking beats summarization in a lot of cases, but it can get expensive as context grows. The post presents a solution where a fork keeps the parts of a conversation it needs and drops the rest.
articles.one-liner: Delegating tasks to subagents via summarization often leads to information loss, suggesting that forking the entire conversation history is often more reliable.

summary.what: The author argues that subagent summarization causes 'theory of mind' failures, and proposes 'smart forks' that use classification models to intelligently prune irrelevant history from subagent contexts.
summary.why: AI developers are learning that efficient agentic workflows require managing context as a limited resource rather than relying on lossy text summaries generated by the agents themselves.
summary.takeaway: If you are building agentic systems, replace full conversation summaries for subagents with 'smart forks' that programmatically filter relevant chunks of context using a secondary classification model.

articles.deep-summary:
* Subagents relying on summaries often ignore intent, decisions, and past corrections.
* Forking provides full context but can become expensive and prone to context-window bloat.
* 'Smart forks' use lightweight classification models to keep only relevant parts of the conversation transcript.
* Theory of mind is a major bottleneck; agents struggle to understand what a subagent lacks without explicit context.
* Pruning irrelevant chunks is more effective than writing lossy summaries for downstream workers.
articles.decoder:
* **System One model**: Refers to faster, cheaper AI models optimized for classification and rapid decision-making rather than generative text production.
* **Theory of mind**: The cognitive ability to understand that other agents have different information, beliefs, and knowledge than one's self.

articles.title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions
articles.description: The Gemini Decisions API can evaluate up to 1,000 yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring questions in a fast, single pass. It can accept text, images, audio, video, and PDF input. Powered by Google's new Gemini Decision 1 model, the model is available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio. It costs $0.10 per 2 million tokens - outputs are free.
articles.one-liner: Google's new Gemini Decisions API allows developers to perform high-speed multimodal classification and rubric scoring at $0.10 per 1M tokens.

summary.what: The Decisions API uses the Gemini Decision 1 model to process text, audio, image, and video inputs to return confidence scores for yes/no, multiple choice, and rubric questions in 150-250 ms.
summary.why: This moves AI usage away from expensive, token-heavy generation toward low-latency 'control plane' tasks like model routing, policy enforcement, and intent classification.
summary.takeaway: Use the Gemini Decisions API in Google AI Studio if you need to perform high-throughput, multimodal classification without the latency of token-by-token generation.

articles.deep-summary:
* Evaluates up to 1,000 independent questions per request in a single forward pass.
* Pricing is $0.10 per 1M input tokens, with no output-token charges.
* Outputs include normalized probabilities and confidence scores for each choice.
* Supports rubric scoring (ordered grading) and noul (binary yes/no).
* Optimized for latency, intended for routing, content grading, and safety checks.
articles.decoder: * **Control plane**: In software architecture, the part of a system that handles routing, management, and decision-making logic rather than the core data processing.

articles.title: The fall of “what you can do” and the rise of “who you know”
articles.description: The returns from being social have gone up. Many well-connected people mix their work and personal lives. Sam Altman is a prime example of a well-connected person who mixes work and personal. He didn't make his connections because he knew they would pay off in his career - he's just a generous person who is innately curious about people and technology. The best strategy is to be your best and truest self.
articles.one-liner: As technical execution becomes commoditized by AI, professional success is shifting from individual output toward social capital and reputation.

summary.what: Jason Wei argues that the rise of AI agents has commoditized research and coding, reducing the competitive advantage of raw output. He suggests that personal connections, trust, and reputation are becoming more critical than technical skill alone, citing OpenAI's Sam Altman as a case study in building value through social networks.
summary.why: The democratization of technical tasks via AI means that when technical output is difficult to independently audit, professional outcomes increasingly rely on non-technical signals like personal endorsements.

articles.title: Of Miracles and Moats
articles.description: AI may simultaneously accelerate imitation and the accumulation of advantage. It is the presence or absence of durable competitive advantage, and the entry price, that determines whether a business and its investors will profit from the proliferation of a technology. More miraculous technologies require better moats. We are entering an age of consumer surplus the likes of which humanity has never seen.
articles.one-liner: History suggests that while miracle technologies like AI create immense value for consumers, the producers often suffer from catastrophic capital cycles and oversupply.

summary.what: Packy McCormick analyzes AI through the lens of historical technological surges like railroads, fiber optics, and oil. He highlights that Anthropic has committed nearly $900 billion in compute through 2045, noting that in winner-take-all markets with high capital intensity, the primary challenge is establishing a 'moat' to prevent competition from commoditizing the service.
summary.why: This reveals the danger of 'miracles without moats' where capital floods an obvious opportunity, eventually crushing margins for everyone except the end consumer who benefits from drastically lower prices.

articles.decoder: * **Consumer Surplus**: The economic gain achieved when consumers are able to purchase a product for a price that is less than the highest price they would be willing to pay.

articles.title: Welcome to the B2A Economy
articles.description: Businesses that treat agents as first-class customers have a shot at a wave of growth.
articles.one-liner: As AI agents increasingly handle web traffic and transactions, businesses are shifting from blocking bots to actively competing for agentic commerce.

summary.what: Olivia and Justine Moore detail the rise of the 'B2A' (Business-to-Agent) economy, where agents like those in ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok increasingly influence purchasing and tool selection. Statistics show AI-referred traffic has higher conversion rates, and platforms like Shopify and Stripe are seeing significant shifts in automated usage.
summary.why: This represents a fundamental change in distribution where the end-user is often not a human, necessitating new strategies for search optimization and API-level access to compete for non-human customers.

articles.deep-summary:
* Agents now drive significant traffic to digital products, with AI-referred shoppers converting better than human-directed ones.
* Platforms are shifting from building anti-bot walls to providing 'connectors' (MCPs) and business feeds to capture agent attention.
* Coding agents have fundamentally changed development workflows, with 40% of GitHub PRs starting as AI drafts.
* Future winners will include companies that optimize their infrastructure for machine-to-machine interactions.
articles.decoder:
* **GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)**: The practice of optimizing content to be prioritized by AI-driven search and conversational engines rather than traditional keyword-based search engines.
* **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**: An open standard that allows AI assistants to connect to data sources and tools directly, enabling standardized integration between models and software.

articles.title: Yes, you should panic about AI
articles.description: Today's models could already transform science and medicine for decades, so a slowdown in AI research would cost much less than you'd think.
articles.one-liner: Rutger Bregman argues that AI's potential to fundamentally accelerate science and medicine warrants a precautionary approach to current research trajectories.

summary.what: Rutger Bregman contends that since current models could transform scientific fields for decades to come, the immediate economic cost of slowing down research is smaller than the potential long-term risks.

articles.title: Who Captures the Most Margin in AI?
articles.description: At a 40% application margin, applications (40%), neoclouds (28%), and inference vendors (24%) capture 92% of total gross profit before GPU depreciation.
articles.one-liner: Analysis of the AI value chain reveals that applications, neoclouds, and inference vendors capture over 90% of gross profit, with heavy vertical integration ongoing.

summary.what: Tomasz Tunguz breaks down AI margins into a normalized '$ per watt per year' metric, showing that AI applications capture 40% of the value, followed by neoclouds (28%) and inference vendors (24%). He notes that firms like CoreWeave are aggressively acquiring software companies to move up the value chain.
summary.why: As GPU compute costs climb and become more standardized, players are aggressively moving into adjacent stack layers to lock in margins and defend against commoditization.

articles.deep-summary:
* The AI stack consists of: Power, Data Center, Neocloud, Inference, and Applications.
* Compute costs are rising, with CoreWeave contracts shifting significantly in pricing per megawatt.
* Gross profit is highly concentrated in the top three layers of the stack.
* Vertical integration (e.g., CoreWeave acquiring Weights & Biases) is the current strategy to protect margins from volatility.
articles.decoder:
* **Neocloud**: Specialized cloud providers, such as CoreWeave or Nebius, that focus specifically on providing GPU-intensive infrastructure rather than general-purpose cloud services like AWS.
* **$/w/yr**: A unit of measurement that normalizes different pricing models (kWh, monthly rent, GPU-hour, task-based) into an annual dollar value per utilized watt of power.

articles.title: The answer to AI is engineering
articles.description: Optimizing for incident response times speeds up build times too.
articles.one-liner: Geoffrey Huntley argues that engineering, specifically via reproducible environments like Nix, is the only sustainable response to the rapid rise of agent-driven security vulnerabilities.

summary.what: Geoffrey Huntley advocates for 'patching the planet' using Nix overlays to maintain a single source of truth for software dependencies. He demonstrates how to use AI agents to monkey-patch vulnerabilities locally across an entire fleet, bypassing slow upstream maintainer updates.
summary.why: Security incidents are accelerating as agents autonomously exploit vulnerabilities; standard open-source dependency management is too fragile and slow to handle this new scale of threat.
summary.takeaway: Clone the 'nix-demo' repository on GitHub to experiment with using Nix to manage environment drift and apply custom patches to transitive dependencies.

articles.deep-summary:
* Security 'take-off' is the new normal, requiring more inferencing capacity to defend than attackers use to exploit.
* Standard open-source library consumption is becoming obsolete as AI can generate first-party replacements faster than patching upstream dependencies.
* Nix provides a single, reproducible source of truth for developer laptops, CI/CD, and production Docker images.
* Agentic sandboxes should be treated as ephemeral and tested using NixOS integration tests.
* Property-based testing (e.g., Hypothesis, Hegel) should replace human-written unit tests to ensure software behavior under extreme edge cases.
articles.decoder:
* **Nix Overlay**: A mechanism in the Nix package manager that allows developers to override or patch packages in a way that affects all transitive dependencies within an environment.
* **Property-based testing**: A testing methodology where generators create random data based on defined properties (rules) for code, rather than static input/output test cases.
* **Monkey-patch**: A technique to extend or modify the runtime behavior of existing software components without changing the original source code.

articles.title: The levels of agentic engineering
articles.description: Look at what people are still doing by hand to figure out where your team is.
articles.one-liner: Transitioning to agentic engineering is not about upgrading tools, but systematically identifying and automating every task you currently perform by hand.

summary.what: Zach Wills, an engineering lead, outlines a seven-level framework for automating software delivery, moving from local AI-assisted coding to multiplayer, cloud-based autonomous factories that handle everything from ticket intake to production verification.
summary.why: This framework shifts the engineering focus from individual feature development to system design, where the primary value lies in building the 'factory' that automates software lifecycle management.
summary.takeaway: To assess your team's current state, manually ship a roadmap item using agents and identify the specific steps that forced you to intervene; those friction points are your next automation targets.

articles.deep-summary:
* Level 1: Offload coding tasks to agents by providing tickets instead of instructions.
* Level 2: Enable autonomous navigation by adding lean architectural pointers (like CLAUDE.md) rather than overly restrictive documentation.
* Level 3: Offload testing and verification by granting agents access to logs, end-to-end testing frameworks, and CI/CD pipelines.
* Level 4: Move execution from local machines to cloud-based runners triggered by external events like tickets or alerts.
* Level 5: Close the loop by having agents verify production outcomes against business goals.
* Level 6: Shift the team's role to maintain and improve the factory system, making the workflow collaborative.
* Level 7: Transition the engineering team's focus entirely to product strategy once the delivery system is fully automated.
articles.decoder:
* **Agentic Engineering**: A software development paradigm where AI agents perform end-to-end tasks, such as coding, testing, and deployment, with minimal human intervention.
* **Claude Code**: A CLI tool that allows LLMs to interact directly with a developer's local environment, filesystem, and terminal.
* **CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment)**: The automated process of testing and deploying code changes to production environments.
* **Greenfield Prototype**: A project built from scratch without existing technical debt or legacy constraints.

articles.title: Companies Dole Out Mega Paydays and Luxury Trips to Compete for AI Talent
articles.description: AI startup Serval is offering a $30,000 signing bonus and a $10,000 vacation to compete for software engineers and deployment strategists.
articles.one-liner: Startups are escalating recruitment incentives for AI talent, offering massive signing bonuses and luxury travel packages to secure experienced engineers and strategists.

summary.what: Companies like Serval are now offering $30,000 signing bonuses and $10,000 vacation incentives to win over specialized engineers, reflecting a hyper-competitive market for AI personnel.
summary.why: The scarcity of specialized AI expertise is forcing firms to innovate on compensation packages, moving beyond standard salary and equity to include experiential perks to differentiate themselves.

articles.title: What's new in Grok Bot 1.0
articles.description: Grok Bot 1.0 adds Team Bots you can publish and share, Slack and Microsoft Teams, meetings on Meet and Zoom, shared connectors, and reviewed learnings. It is now a personal assistant that the whole team can talk to in the app, in Slack, in Microsoft Teams, and in video calls. This post covers how to create a Team Bot and publish it, how to bring the bot into Microsoft Teams, how to add a bot to a meeting, and more. It also looks at the new admin controls and what's possible without a team.
articles.one-liner: Grok Bot 1.0 evolves into a shared team assistant with integrations for Slack, Microsoft Teams, and video conferencing platforms.

summary.what: Grok Bot 1.0 introduces Team Bots, enabling collaborative access within Slack, Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and Google Meet, alongside updated admin controls for managing team-wide knowledge.

articles.title: Runway Praxis-1 Is Now Available: Open-Weight Robotics Model
articles.description: Runway's Praxis-1, a 27B-parameter open-weight robotics model, is now available under Apache 2.0. The model excels in predicting video and actions, topping NVIDIA's RoboLab-120 leaderboard with a 46.2% success rate across 1,200 episodes. It's accessible on GitHub and Hugging Face, with support for full and LoRA fine-tuning, compatible with NVIDIA hardware, and adaptable for various robotic embodiments.
articles.one-liner: Runway has released Praxis-1, a 27B-parameter open-weight world action model for robotics, under the Apache 2.0 license.

summary.what: Praxis-1 is a diffusion-based model that predicts both video and actions. It outperforms models like FLUX 3 Action and π0.5 on the RoboLab-120 benchmark and supports fine-tuning via LoRA on NVIDIA hardware.
summary.why: Releasing high-performing world models with open weights lowers the barrier for robotics developers to deploy frontier AI capabilities on custom hardware embodiments.
summary.takeaway: Test Praxis-1 on your robot using the LeRobot integration on Hugging Face or via the GitHub repository.

articles.deep-summary:
* 27B-parameter mixture-of-experts diffusion transformer architecture
* Apache 2.0 licensed for commercial use
* Outperforms FLUX 3 Action (46.2% vs 42.9% success on RoboLab-120)
* Supports full fine-tuning and LoRA
* Compatible with NVIDIA H100, B200, RTX 5090, and Jetson Thor hardware
* Training data leverages web video alongside teleoperated robot data
articles.decoder:
* **LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)**: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique that freezes pretrained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices, significantly reducing memory requirements.
* **World Action Model**: A model trained to predict future video frames and corresponding physical actions in a 3D environment.
* **Embodiment**: The specific physical form of a robot (e.g., legged, industrial arm) in which the AI policy is deployed.

articles.title: Escaping SPACE: Part II
articles.description: Perplexity tested 12 models against its SPACE agent sandbox: none escaped VM-host isolation, but several bypassed network controls through DNS spoofing and shared-IP exploitation before the flaws were fixed. The experiments also found that capture-the-flag prompts distracted agents from the security boundary being tested.
articles.one-liner: Perplexity’s red-teaming experiments show that frontier models struggle to escape sandbox isolation, while cybersecurity-focused models often underperform on systemic vulnerabilities compared to general models.

summary.what: Perplexity tested 12 models in its SPACE sandbox; none escaped VM isolation, but models bypassed network controls using DNS spoofing and IP-sharing. Specialized cybersecurity models like GPT-5.6 Cyber performed worse than general-purpose models like GPT-5.6 Sol.
summary.why: Cybersecurity specialization in LLMs may create narrow problem-solving biases that overlook unconventional design-level vulnerabilities, suggesting a need for more diverse training data.

articles.deep-summary:
* Evaluated 12 models: Claude Opus/Mythos, DeepSeek V4, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GLM 5.2, GPT-5.6/6, Grok 4.20, Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8
* VM-host isolation remained secure; network egress controls were vulnerable to DNS spoofing and IP-sharing
* Capture-the-Flag (CTF) prompts often distracted agents from security boundaries; focused prompts yielded better evaluation data
* GPT-6 Astra and Claude Mythos 5.1 showed the strongest reasoning capabilities across trajectories
* Cybersecurity-specialized training may lead to narrow "bug-hunting" strategies instead of broader system-level analysis
articles.decoder:
* **Egress control**: Network security policy that restricts the traffic that can leave a protected environment (like a sandbox).
* **DNS spoofing**: An attack where an agent returns a forged DNS response to map an allowed domain to a malicious IP address.
* **Domain fronting**: An obfuscation technique where the SNI (Server Name Indication) and HTTP Host headers differ, allowing traffic to bypass domain-based egress filters.

articles.title: MCP vs CLI vs Skills: What Each Costs in Context
articles.description: MCP servers significantly increase token use, adding thousands of input tokens per request, unlike CLI or skill methods. On Sonnet 5.5, a simple task showed MCP consuming 59,417 tokens with default tools against CLI's 1,421 and skill's 3,315, highlighting the high cost of tool-heavy MCP setups. Implementing Tool Search can cut token costs by deferring tool definitions, reducing upfront toolset costs to under 600 tokens for optimal efficiency.
articles.one-liner: Using MCP servers for AI agents can balloon token costs by thousands; deferring tool definitions via Tool Search is a necessary optimization.

summary.what: The GitHub MCP server with 46 default tools adds ~19,000 input tokens per request. Using OpenRouter's Tool Search to defer definitions can reduce upfront costs to under 600 tokens.
summary.why: High token overhead in MCP tool-calling limits agent efficiency; moving to scoped toolsets or lazy loading is essential for cost-effective production AI agents.
summary.takeaway: Add "defer_loading": true to your MCP tool configurations and implement "openrouter:tool_search" to minimize context window bloat.

articles.deep-summary:
* MCP servers load all tool schemas into the model context by default
* A simple GitHub task used 59,417 tokens with MCP compared to 1,421 with a direct CLI
* Tool results (e.g., large JSON objects) often cost more than the definitions themselves
* Tool Search allows models to search and load only required tools on demand
* CLI tools remain the most efficient if the model is well-trained on them; MCP is best when auth/permissions are required
articles.decoder:
* **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**: An open standard for connecting AI assistants to data and tools.
* **Token inflation**: The phenomenon where providing extensive tool definitions consumes a large percentage of an LLM's available context window.

articles.title: LLMs can learn some multi-step reasoning on filler tokens instead of visible CoT
articles.description: By changing the training setup and applying LoRAs to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and gpt-oss-20b, researchers taught models to do some multi-step tasks while emitting only filler tokens, beating an answer-only baseline on three of seven tasks. They also mapped theoretical layer-depth limits and showed empirical walls, with some tasks learned out to 60 steps and others failing after one to three. The work is meant to separate filler-token reasoning from steganographic hidden reasoning when interpreting chain-of-thought.
articles.one-liner: Researchers demonstrated that LLMs can perform multi-step reasoning using hidden internal states via 'filler tokens' without needing to output coherent chain-of-thought text.

summary.what: By training Qwen3.6 and gpt-oss-20b with LoRAs, researchers successfully taught models to solve multi-step tasks using filler dot sequences, bypassing the need for standard reasoning outputs.
summary.why: This challenges the assumption that reasoning is strictly tied to visible chain-of-thought, implying that hidden reasoning could eventually threaten the monitorability of AI systems.

articles.deep-summary:
* Filler-token reasoning: model uses extra tokens to reason internally without emitting relevant words
* Demonstrated feasibility on tasks including Mod Sum, GL(3,2), and ProntoQA
* Used LoRA fine-tuning with a curriculum of increasing task length
* Theory shows some tasks require deeper algorithmic circuits, setting empirical walls for model performance
* Challenges standard interpretability assumptions that equate 'thinking' with visible 'chain-of-thought'
articles.decoder:
* **Filler tokens**: Tokens emitted by a model (like '.' or '_') that carry no explicit semantic meaning but provide the model with computation steps.
* **Steganographic reasoning**: A hypothesis where models perform reasoning internally while emitting innocuous-looking text to hide the process.
* **TC⁰**: A complexity class representing problems solvable by circuits of constant depth; conceptually, parallelizable tasks.

articles.title: Don't Write Kernels, Derive Them
articles.description: Current models rely on hand-written kernels specific to operators, chips, and fusions, limiting flexibility across devices and scenarios. Tang's IR enables on-the-fly derivation of kernels through constructs such as views and comprehensions, eliminating the need for pre-defined kernels.
articles.one-liner: Tang replaces hand-written operator kernels with an IR that derives and fuses kernels on-the-fly, allowing performance parity with expert-tuned engines.

summary.what: Tang's tensor IR uses views and comprehensions to derive fused kernels at runtime. It matches the performance of hand-tuned engines like those for 80B MoE models on H200s by replacing operator-specific code with algebraic rewrites.
summary.why: The shift from manual kernel writing to derived kernels moves the burden of optimization from humans to compilers, enabling better performance across diverse hardware without specialized library maintenance.

articles.deep-summary:
* IR constructs: Views (affine maps) and Comprehensions (reductions over a monoid)
* Derived kernels outperform hand-written ones in specific regimes by eliminating materialized intermediate buffers
* Fusion is treated as a single substitution rewrite rule; flash attention is derived, not hardcoded
* Backward pass is generated automatically via reverse-mode differentiation of comprehensions
* Supports multiple targets: CUDA, WGSL, Metal, C, OpenCL, and GLSL
* Validated on M4 Max, RTX 3090, H200, and Android-based humanoid robot SoC
articles.decoder:
* **Monoid**: A mathematical structure used here to define how reduction operations (like sum or max) are combined.
* **Affine Map**: A transformation used in views to express memory access patterns like transposes or slices without explicit pointer arithmetic.
* **FlashAttention**: A memory-efficient attention mechanism that computes attention scores in blocks to minimize memory traffic.

articles.title: AlphaGenome 2: Predicting how DNA shapes cells and disease
articles.description: AlphaGenome 2 improves prediction of DNA variant effects on specific cell types, aiding in disease understanding and research. It doubles variant identification compared to its predecessor and adapts to analyze new cell states without retraining. Available for non-commercial use, the tool bridges genetics and cell biology, pinpointing disease-relevant genetic mutations in primary human cells.
articles.one-liner: AlphaGenome 2 is a new conditional DNA model that predicts how specific genetic variants affect gene expression across hundreds of human cell types.

summary.what: Developed by Google DeepMind researchers including Adam Gayoso and Žiga Avsec, AlphaGenome 2 uses a conditional architecture to predict gene regulation, chromatin accessibility, and DNA methylation. It identified nearly twice as many causal variants (30%) compared to its predecessor in a study of 28 immune cell types. The model is available for non-commercial research via API.
summary.why: By transitioning from bulk tissue averages to cell-type-specific predictions, this model enables more precise identification of disease-causing mutations, which is critical for drug discovery.
summary.takeaway: If you are conducting non-commercial genomics research, you can access the model today through the AlphaGenome API.

articles.deep-summary:
* **Conditional Modeling**: Unlike its predecessor, AlphaGenome 2 takes specific cell-type conditions as input, allowing it to adapt to new, unseen cell states without retraining.
* **Cross-modality Imputation**: It can predict missing experimental properties (like chromatin accessibility) based on a single measurement, helping prioritize further experiments.
* **Enhanced Recall**: It improves the identification of causal variants by resolving activity within specialized cells rather than relying on tissue-wide averages.
* **Non-commercial Access**: The tool is currently available for academic research, with a commercial preview in progress.
articles.decoder:
* **Chromatin Accessibility**: The extent to which DNA is available for transcription machinery to access and read the genetic code.
* **GWAS (Genome-Wide Association Study)**: An observational study of a genome-wide set of genetic variants in different individuals to see if any variant is associated with a trait.

articles.title: OpenAI open-sources MCP Extensions for ChatGPT-native plugins
articles.description: The TypeScript and Python packages add ChatGPT-specific features to MCP servers and apps, including sidebar entry points, custom file viewers, composer resource search, and thumbnail part pickers. The SDKs ship with a Bits & Bolts demo plugin and a written spec.
articles.one-liner: OpenAI open-sourced MCP Extensions to help developers build ChatGPT plugins that integrate directly with native UI features like sidebars and custom file viewers.

summary.what: The new TypeScript and Python SDKs allow developers to build plugins for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) that include sidebar entry points, composer resource search, and thumbnail pickers. A demo plugin, Bits & Bolts, is provided to demonstrate these native-feeling UI capabilities.
summary.why: This signals OpenAI’s shift toward making third-party AI agents feel like first-class citizens within the ChatGPT interface, improving user experience by moving beyond simple text-only responses.
summary.takeaway: If you are building MCP servers, check the `docs/spec.md` in the GitHub repo to implement native UI extensions for your agents.

articles.decoder: * **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**: An open standard that enables AI models to connect securely to local or remote data sources and tools.

articles.title: A2UI 1.0: Build delightful, fast, reliable, agentic experiences
articles.description: A2UI is an open protocol for generative UI that lets agents answer with interactive screens. Open-source renderer SDKs are now available for the web, Android, iOS, and agent SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and Dart. A2UI enables apps to draw UIs with native components, securely. Users get the same low latency, high trust, and complete native fidelity whether they reach a company's agent in its own app or in a third-party AI assistant that hosts MCP apps.
articles.one-liner: A2UI 1.0 launches as an open protocol for generative UI, enabling AI agents to render interactive, native-speed components across mobile and web platforms.

summary.what: Led by Google's Vishal Motwani, A2UI 1.0 provides renderer SDKs for React, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose. Companies like Atlassian and Alation are using it to render interactive metric cards and forms directly within AI assistant interfaces like Claude and Gemini.
summary.why: The industry is moving toward 'generative UI,' where agents no longer just provide text but offer functional, interactive interfaces to complete tasks immediately.
summary.takeaway: Try the A2UI Playground by CopilotKit to see how your agent can render interactive components natively.

articles.deep-summary:
* **Bidirectional Function Calls**: Version 1.0 allows for real-time interaction, such as checking flight availability directly within a generated UI card.
* **Platform Agnostic**: Uses renderer libraries to draw components natively, ensuring brand consistency across web, iOS, and Android.
* **Security**: Sensitive data stays on the server, as the UI binds to data locally rather than passing it through the LLM.
* **Integration**: Compatible with MCP Apps, allowing A2UI-powered screens to appear in third-party assistants.
articles.decoder: * **Generative UI**: An emerging UI paradigm where an AI model dynamically generates interface components based on user intent rather than relying on static, pre-defined screens.

articles.title: Shopify's generative discovery model
articles.description: Shopify deployed a shared generative discovery model for search and recommendation, leveraging semantic-ID tokens to enhance product personalization and relevance. The model improved online and offline metrics, such as a 9.85% lift in conversion rate and significant gains in search relevance.
articles.one-liner: Shopify achieved a 9.85% increase in conversion rates by deploying a shared generative discovery model for search and recommendation.

summary.what: Shopify used Liquid AI’s LFM2-2.6B model to power search and recommendations. By mapping products to 3-token semantic IDs using RQ-KMeans clustering, the team reduced the vocabulary complexity required to represent billions of products, improving both relevance and serving latency.
summary.why: This architecture demonstrates how to efficiently apply large models to massive catalogs by moving from raw ID lookups to semantic-based token generation.

articles.deep-summary:
* **Semantic-ID Tokens**: Products are represented as short sequences of discrete codes (semantic IDs) generated via RQ-KMeans clustering, enabling the model to learn representations for products with few interactions.
* **Multi-teacher Distillation**: The team trained specialized search and recommendation experts and then distilled their capabilities into a single, efficient student model.
* **Constrained Decoding**: Using a custom CUDA/C++ plugin within TurboMind, Shopify reduced the overhead of ensuring the model only generates valid product paths from over 50ms to approximately 1ms per request.
* **Multi-token Prediction (MTP)**: The model predicts tokens in parallel rather than autoregressively, allowing for faster candidate generation.
articles.decoder:
* **RQ-KMeans**: Residual Quantized K-Means; a method used to iteratively cluster product embeddings into discrete codes, capturing hierarchical information.
* **OneDCG@10**: A search metric (variant of NDCG) that normalizes search relevance against a reference point of ten perfect results.

articles.title: Browser use has been rolling out in Antigravity
articles.description: Browser use in Antigravity closes the loop between researching, writing code, and verifying it live. Users control authentication, and downloads pause until they are approved. Agents can use the browser to run multiple tasks at once. A video demo is available in the post.
articles.one-liner: Antigravity has integrated browser-use capabilities, allowing agents to perform live research and verify code directly in a web environment.

summary.what: The feature enables agents to handle multi-task browsing, with user-controlled authentication and manual approval required for file downloads. This closes the loop for developers by letting the agent browse the web, write code, and test it in real-time.
summary.why: Giving agents autonomous web access significantly increases their utility for complex engineering workflows, though it introduces new security considerations for authenticated sessions.
summary.takeaway: Try the feature in Antigravity today; ensure you are monitoring your agent's activity regarding file downloads.

articles.title: United moves to block AI agents
articles.description: United Airlines is moving to restrict AI-agent access across its platforms and agency channels, citing credential security and liability risks around tasks such as check-in. The restrictions contrast with travel companies including Expedia and Booking that are partnering with agents.
articles.one-liner: United Airlines is restricting AI agents from its digital platforms, citing security risks and potential liability for automated tasks like flight check-ins.

summary.what: The airline intends to update its booking and ticketing policies to block AI bots that access customer accounts, warning users that sharing credentials with third-party assistants risks unauthorized account changes and use of miles. This marks a divergence from competitors like Expedia, which are actively integrating AI agents.
summary.why: A clear conflict is emerging between consumer-facing AI agents that seek to automate travel tasks and the underlying infrastructure providers that prioritize platform security and regulatory compliance.

articles.title: Google Tabletop Creates Shared Interactive Planning Spaces
articles.description: Google Labs' Tabletop turns links, files, and prompts into interactive itineraries, polls, expense splitters, and tournament brackets.
articles.one-liner: Google Labs is testing Tabletop, a collaborative canvas that turns files and prompts into structured formats like itineraries and brackets.

summary.what: Tabletop is a new collaborative tool from Google Labs that generates interactive objects like polls, expense splitters, and tournament brackets from user input. It is currently rolling out in the U.S. via a waitlist.
summary.why: The tool aims to bridge the gap between static group chats and specialized planning software by offering a flexible, document-like interface for ad-hoc group logistics.
summary.takeaway: Sign up for the waitlist at labs.google/tabletop if you want to experiment with creating shared collaborative spaces.

articles.title: ElevenAI (Website)
articles.description: ElevenAI is a desktop app that helps amplify work using agents.
articles.one-liner: ElevenLabs is expanding into desktop agents with ElevenAI, a Mac-based tool for meeting transcription, dictation, and automated workflow handoffs.

summary.what: ElevenAI is a new desktop application that provides system-wide dictation, automated meeting summaries, and agentic integrations via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It features on-device transcript storage and holds SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO/IEC 27001 security certifications.
summary.why: By moving from specialized speech synthesis to a broad agentic platform, ElevenLabs is shifting from being a content creation tool to a utility for enterprise workflow automation.

articles.deep-summary:
* **Transcription & Dictation**: Supports 90+ languages with automatic filler word removal and punctuation.
* **Integration**: Uses MCP to connect meeting notes and transcripts to third-party tools.
* **Security**: Transcripts are stored locally; the company claims not to store audio files.
* **Deployment**: Supports both individual self-service and managed enterprise-wide rollouts.
articles.decoder: * **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**: An open standard developed by Anthropic that allows AI assistants to securely connect to data sources and developer tools.

articles.title: OpenAI wants agents to tell websites where you are
articles.description: Two OpenAI engineers recently shared a proposal that suggests a change that will let agents pass user information along to websites to make them look like normal visitors rather than bots.
articles.one-liner: An OpenAI proposal to send user network signals to websites is drawing sharp criticism for potential privacy leaks and insufficient authentication.

summary.what: Two OpenAI engineers proposed an Internet-Draft (draft-panero-httpbis-forwarded-user-signals) that would allow AI agents to pass information like IP-country, locale, and time zone to websites to bypass bot detection. Critic Joost Baaij argues the draft lacks proper signatures, risks privacy, and creates caching inefficiencies.
summary.why: This signals an ongoing friction between AI agent operators, who need to appear 'human' to avoid blocks, and web standards, which were designed for direct human-to-server interaction.

articles.deep-summary:
* **The Problem**: Agents are frequently blocked because they appear to originate from known data center IP ranges.
* **The Proposal**: Add six parameters (asn, ip-country, ip-prefix, locale, tz, user-agent) to the standard Forwarded header.
* **Security Risk**: The draft suggests signatures are optional, which could allow malicious actors to spoof legitimate residential network identities.
* **Caching Impact**: Adding dynamic user data to request headers risks breaking server-side caching if not implemented with a Vary header.
* **Privacy Concern**: The combination of these signals creates a browser fingerprint, which could be exploited for tracking.
articles.decoder:
* **Forwarded Header**: A standard HTTP header used to identify the endpoints of a proxy chain, often used to reveal the original client IP to the destination server.
* **Client Hints**: An extension to HTTP that allows servers to negotiate which information about a client's device/preferences they want the browser to send.

articles.title: Nvidia board reportedly preparing to oust Huang
articles.description: Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang following his admission of an affair with a woman US intelligence agencies believe was recruited by Chinese intelligence.

articles.title: Databricks Genie Agents
articles.description: Databricks Genie Agents can now analyze unstructured documents alongside database tables, connect to enterprise tools, and share insights externally with governance controls.
articles.one-liner: Databricks Genie Agents can now reason over unstructured documents and connect directly to enterprise apps to perform automated actions.

summary.what: Databricks expanded its Genie Agents to include public preview support for unstructured data (PDFs, slides) and general availability for MCP connectors to Jira, Slack, and Google Drive. It also introduced OpenSharing and Genie Clean Rooms for governed cross-organization collaboration.
summary.why: Databricks is trying to position the Data Lakehouse as the primary orchestration layer for AI agents, moving them beyond SQL queries into operational, multi-tool workflows that respect enterprise governance.

articles.deep-summary:

articles.decoder:
